review_text: “A well kept secret in downtown.” We stayed at this hotel on October 1st, 2012. What a gorgeous place to stay. I had requested a room facing the canal, which even though it was raining was a great view. Katie on the front desk when we checked in was super, super kind & helpful. The hotel was in a quiet area of downtown, and I'd dare say a safe area as we walked, (our own choosing), to a restaurant down by the Capitol building. It was a very clean hotel and the bed was quite comfortable as well. Now that we know this hotel is here, we'll take the extra time to get off the interstate and go downtown for sure.

“Great hotel” I have stayed here twice recently on business and had great experiences both times. It is very clean and the rooms are perfect, with full-sized refrigerator, microwave and stove top. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The manager's reception was perfect for dinner, since I
 was working, I didn't have time to go out. The breakfast was fine--not the best, but good enough. I have recommended the hotel to some of my colleagues and they were very satisfied with the hotel also. Will always stay here when I come to Indianapolis.

“Feels like Home!” The staff are so friendly (you can tell that they are super well trained to focus on customers!). The Happy Hours are a nice touch and the food both nights that I was there was good and could easily serve as dinner. The breakfast was not as good to me as other reviewers stated, however it was fast, complimentary, and filling. The only negative (a fairly big one!) was that my room was not cleaned after the first night. I put a "do not disturb" sign on my door at about 10pm and removed at 830am when I left for the day. When I got back around 5pm or so, the room was not cleaned yet (that happens sometimes) and I left again only to return at 10pm to an uncleaned room. I had plenty of towels, and nothing was really dirty plus I wanted to go to bed so I did not call housekeeping. I am not sure what their check system is, but it failed for my room.

“Very convenient location!” If you have business in downtown Indianapolis, this Residence Inn is very clean and convenient. The staff is very friendly, greeted this weary traveler warmly and my room was ready and clean.
Unlike many Residence Inns, the breakfast buffet is spread out a bit. The bagel and muffin stations are in two distinct areas with separate toasters. Seems like a trivial detail but that is a feature I notice as I stay at this chain quite often and see the backup at other locations. Great idea!
One feature that would be nice to have here would be automatic doors at the lobby. I noticed folks with large bags struggling to open the doors.
Given the price difference between here and the JW Marriott who probably have the automatic doors but no free breakfast, I will stay here again!

“Add me to the list: a great property on Indy's Canal” A great stay. Had room on 4th floor facing the canal. You get your own apartment at a Residence Inn--and this property is no exception. Staff was top notch. Room was spotless. Did NOT need vacuming like many hotel rooms do. And a full 6+ coffee maker--not the downsized versions found these days in most hotels that make just 1 cup. Full kitchen. Microwave popcorn. Free weights in the weight room. One free Uniguest computer. And unlike most hotels which have HD TVs but not HD channels--this property has the traditional TV. Ask for a room facing the canal. And if it is a weekend avoid the outrageous $17 parking charge and park on the street. Walk to the mall and nearrby restaurants--a cab is hardly needed.

“Stayed here for a couple nights” First, what a location. You are right on the canal, and it is amazing. Great place to walk, clean, safe, etc... It's a fairly new development as most of the buildings are new. If you have an afternoon to yourself, bring your walking shoes, plenty to do around the canal.
The hotel itself, not bad. The staff could not be friendlier, and the hotel is clean. Two issues: TVs are very small and ancient, and elevators are painfully slow. Ask for a room near the stairwell as it's much quicker to walk. 
Free hot breakfast. Paking is $17 a day. Safe area. Got it for $45 on night on Priceline. Bourbon Street bar is a block away. Outdoor bar if you are into that. Good greasy food and cold beer.

“Nice, Friendly, Family Hotel” We stayed at the Residence Inn for only one night. The staff was excellent. The rooms were clean. My only slight complaint was that the bed was a little too soft. With the hotel being right on the canal, it was pretty cool to walk out the back entrance and take a morning walk along the canal. Pool was nice too. The variety of item offered for the free hot morning breakfast was good.

“Quite a Lovely View” I stayed here as because of the central location in Indianapolis. The rooms had nice kitchenettes and full size refigerators. The bed was very comfortable and the living room large enough for the three days I was there. The breakfast was up to par with scambled eggs and sausage, fruit, cereal, and yogurt, although these and everything else needed to be replenished more often than it was. If Ihad been on a time crunch, 15 minutes or more to refresh the station items would have been too long for me. The hotel also had a nice pool although small, but a good size jacuzzi. There was also a pool table in the basement. The hotel is right along the canal and a short walk to rent the paddleboats. Some people brought their dogs because the hotel accepts pets for a fee.

“Pretty typical Residence Inn” My family stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown Indianapolis in July to attend Drum Corps events for several days.
The hotel property is on the edge of downtown. It is close enough to walk just about everywhere - 6 blocks to the mall, 6 blocks to the Convention Center, 8 blocks to the new football stadium. Walking seemed safe enough, although I was surprised how many panhandlers are in Indianapolis - probably 2-4 per block right downtown.
The hotel itself is a pretty standard Residence Inn. Our room did show some wear and tear in the kitchen and bath but was pretty clean. Breakfast service was fine, the indoor pool and exercise rooms were small but adequate. Guest laundry worked well and the front desk supplies detergent free of charge.
There were a few negatives - very slow elevators, spotty Wi-Fi service and a fair amount of noise from the parking lot. The hotel also charges about $15 per night for surface parking - in my mind, a bit high for Indianapolis.
Is it the best property in Indy? No, but it was convenient and provided everything we needed downtown. We stayed on points, but I'd feel OK paying up to about $130 a night.

“Great place for an extended stay!” Stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown by the Canal for three weeks. I would not hesistate to stay at this hotel if you're in Indianapolis for extended period of time. The staff really goes out of their way to make you feel at home. The hotel is located conveniently downtown (you are within walking distance from many restaurants and the Circle Center shopping Center), near the free bus routes and cabs are easy to get from the location as well. I was really impressed by the amenities offered: a more than adequate free full breakfast (that included hot items like eggs and sausage) the free wifi throughout the hotel, as well access to a color printer and computer in the lobby. While I didn't use the service, there is a free grocery delivery service available (they just charge the actual price of the groceries on your list to your room bill). My room, located on the second floor by the elevator, was clean and pretty spacious. The only problem I had with the hotel would be the elevator--while there are only 4 floors...it is super slow. Take the stairs instead! 
All in all it was a great stay.

“Good Clean Hotel” My spouse had some minor surgery and this was nearby. The staff was outstanding taking care of us. We needed ice packs and meals brought in to our room, the staff went out of their way to provide freezer help us with the meals. When my spouse fainted in the hall the stall was there on the spot to help. The room was clean and comfortable, the free breakfast was good and the hotel is pet friendly.

“Very Nice Hote,. Close to Galleria Mall” I stayed at thsi hotel on a business trip to Houston. My business was at the Galleria Mall, and this hotel was close by. Very nice hotel, better thyan I expected for a La Quinta Inn. I thought itr was too expensive for the locatio, but I was there during the Houston Rodeo, so maybe the prices were elevated fro that reason. Not convienant for taxis, but all things considered a very enjoyable stay. Very clean room and friendly staff.

“Great place!” Second time we've stayed here. Desk folks were so helpful. Our car was broken into downtown at Astros game. Glass everywhere. Went to desk to ask about a car wash to vacuum up the glass. They got their employe Nathaniel to come and vacuum it out for me! And the desk clerk was so helpful with a glass company referral. AND the hotel is nice. At checkin didn't have any double queens with non smoking, so upgraded to a king suite. NICE, bigger than some apartments. Bed was comfortable, everything super clean, breakfast was normal waffles, pastries, oatmeal, etc.

“Works for me” I'm in Houston for an extended stay and this isnt the first hotel I stayed at in the area. But due to the location and reasonable price I will be staying a while. The rooms are adequate but could use a furniture update. The hotel also got new flat screen tv's as well at first mine wouldnt work and I missed the cowboys game last sunday but they moved me to a new room the next day. However for the highend area this is a good hotel for the price. I would reccomend.

“Stay here alot, but not so good this time” I stay at this facility often and the stay is usually what I expect from LQ. But this time, they let me down.
They gave me a room on the 6th floor.
The room needed some TLC, cleaning and most of all the AC did not work.
It blew lukewarm at best air and made loud moaning noises.
I brought this to the front desk attention and they did move me...right next door, where at least that AC did cool, but made a like moaning noise.
The worst part was there were a number of young people (read teenagers) on the floor and they were VERY nosily and slamming doors, running and very loud.
Since I was there only one night, I tolerated, but will not next time.
The beds were ok in the 2nd room.
Just not up to what I expect from LQ.

“Provided Value and Great Location” Spent 27 days in this hotel with 10 collegues. You can't beat the value or location to the Galleria area. They just remodeled the hotel, great breakfast and large public areas.

“Very Disappointed With This Stay” I stayed at this location last year during the last weekend in October. You will see my previous review below. I enjoyed it so much that I returned again. I made the reservation for myself and a friend several weeks in advance for two beds, non-smoking. 
I arrived at the hotel around 3 pm on Friday, November 6. The front desk clerk asked me if I really needed two beds instead of a king. I said that I need two beds. The other desk clerk chimed in and kept asking me if I absolutely need two beds. I was rather annoyed and said that I needed two beds. End of discussion.
When I checked in my room, I called my friend who was enroute to the hotel. I told him the room number. Minutes later, there was a knock at the door. I thought it was my friend. When I opened up the door, it was the security lady. She just stared at me and I finally asked "May I help you?" She was staring around my body looking through the room. She said rather curtly, "Oh, I'm just checking on the room!". I thought that was rather strange and rude!
When I went to the business area, there was a noticed that the Internet was down. Bummer!
The breakfast was very limited and an awful experience. Last year, there was an ample selections of pastries, etc. This time there were very little to choose from. The few selections that were being offered were not kept stocked and there was no coffee. There was some group that looked like a high school cheerleading team. They totally took over the breakfast area and were practicing in the lobby!. Trash cans were overflowing with trash and it looked like a war zone. I went out to the gazebo in the garden which I really enjoyed last year. The place was trashy all weekend. I mean all weekend! 
Saturday, we were in our room watching TV and there was a knock at the door. There was a couple with their luggage. The wife said, you're in our room! We told them that this was our room and that we checked in last night. We kept the deadbolt locked not knowing what to expect next. 
We skipped the breakfast before check out on Sunday. It was very sparse with boring minimal selections. I stayed at the La Quinta in Mt. Pleasant Texas on Friday, October 23 and the breakfast there was excellent. This breakfast was pathetic! Overall, I was very disappointed at this LaQuinta.

“Value Destination in Upscale Location” I stayed here in early April for 2 nights because all the other hotels in the Galleria area were $200 and up. $130 got me a nice room, the usual ok La Quinta breakfast, and a nice pool area. Computer with free internet access in lobby. There was no hot water one morning because the boiler wasn't working. Overall, a good stay for the price.

“Great Stay Except...” Stayed here in Feb. of 2007. Building and grounds looked nice and inviting, as do most LQ Inn & Suites, so this was as expected.
Check-in took a long time. Usually I'm pretty open-minded if I have a long wait to check in, but this was pretty bad. The receptionist was very nice but she was dealing with another guest for a very long period while I waited. The other guest was asking question after question so I know it wasn't her fault that she couldn't get to me quickly. I did not see any other receptionists so I dismissed this problem as bad timing.
Finally got to my room and checked everything out. Room was clean and it was good to see a fridge (usually found in all LQ Inn & Suites). I then grabbed the ice container and as soon as I moved it, I found one of the biggest roaches I have ever seen in my life. My wife and I went downstairs to let the receptionist know about the problem, and by this time there was another person helping at the front desk who I believe was the manager on duty. She was incredibly gracious and upgraded us to a suite.
We got to the suite and the room key they gave us for the suite did not work, but that was fixed with another visit to the front desk. Once we finally settled in to the new room, everything from that point was perfect. The suite room was perfect, and we didn't see any signs of bugs or roaches from that point on. And since we stayed for 2 nights, we were able to enjoy the upgraded suite for 2 nights without extra charge.
Breakfast each morning was typically good and fine. Bagels and waffles were tasty. I think this location has the Texas-shaped waffle maker.
All in all a great stay. After an unpleasant check-in for 3 different reasons, the service and room during the rest of our stay gave us nothing to complain about.
I would recommend this hotel for anyone in the area, and would stay there again.

“OK place to crash” I stayed at this hotel as part of a bachelor party weekend. Eight guys stayed in four rooms, using the hotel as the launching point for our afternoon and evening exploits. The only really negative thing I have to say is that the breakfast buffet is too loud, and it woke me up (I'd come in at 4 a.m., so that may have been my fault); it could be mitigated if only they would shut the doors to the room hallways on the 2nd floor.
It was clean and centrally located. It was a pretty good value and had Internet access.
We didn't have any surprises. Just beds, showers, locking doors and lots of ice.

“A good hotel for the price” A nice and relatively cheap place to stay in the very center of Manhattan. Great location and easy walk access to numerous sights of interest! I didn't realize that Americana had shared bathrooms at first (missed that in description and never stayed in such inns before), but the suits have sinks and there are lots of bathrooms, so I never had to wait.

“Super depressing” The pictures posted here are of the better rooms.
Good if you're 19 years old and on an adventure around the world, with only a few bucks in your pocket and lots of friend. Otherwise, stay away. One of the more depressing low-budget experiences.

“We loved it and we'll be back (stole this title from TA, LOL)” Just spend 7 nights in the Americana with my niece. I’m a budget traveller and I chose this location for it’s proximity to Bryant Park and was not disappointed, only a 2 minute walk to this little haven of peace in hectic New York.
We were upgraded to a 3 bed room, which for this hotel means a pretty large room! I already posted other pictures earlier and yes, rooms can be pretty cramped.
I’m giving this hotel 5 stars, though, but that is keeping in mind it’s only a one star hotel and we got a pretty good deal, booking it early on a slight discount, and got a wonderful upgrade as mentioned!
Actually, after reading all the reviews I was surprised at the little street noise we experienced. Nothing spectacular, really. Sure, we both used earplugs, but that only drowns noise a little….guess we were both too tired, though I did spend 1 or 2 nights staying up late working on the pc.
No internet in the rooms, as stated, but Bryant Park offers free wifi which is perfect as long as you sit in one of the corners. The park did close at 11 PM, to my surprise.
Pillows were fine though not overly thick, beds a little squeaky, nice firm mattresses (which is how I like them). We experienced no noisy neighbours at all, but that’s always a matter of luck, I think.
No carpets, so no dirty stains, fine by me! Yes, the bathrooms could be damp, as there was no airing system…but when I share bathrooms, I make a point of wearing flipflops at all times! They were clean, though, and water pressure and temperature was good.
About 4 or 5 to each floor, only one with a window…
As for the bedding, the linen was fresh and clean, the blankets thin and indeed had holes in them…they did seem clean to me. 
There was a flatscreen tv, but we never had in on, so I can’t comment on that.
We could actually get on to the fire escape, which we did once to have some tea and it was great fun!
Luckily, we also had a functioning airco, as the outside temperature was well in it’s 80’s! Boy, it was hot in NY that week! As one NY-er we got talking to said: ‘you picked the worst weather ever to visit!’ He was right, of course, but we still had a wonderful trip and the last 2 days the weather gods had some mercy on our souls…
There is a small elevator, no fan or airco inside, so with these temperatures: a free sauna was included. It stops on the second floor at any time, so we opted to take the steps from that floor and back…..I have to admit, not the fastest elevator I know….we sometimes took the stairs down not to get too hot…but, as I mentioned, weather conditions were extreme!
Fire plans, extinguishers, alarms, escapes, all seemed to be in perfect order.
Every floor had one kitchen with a microwave, a cooking device and a fridge. No utensils. 
There is a lovely little deli across the street, run by Chinese, where you could get great stuff (warm food after 11 AM, I think) to take to the park and have breakfast or diner. A small diner across the street which was fine (prêt-a-manger right below, but we didn’t try that), a lovely diner 2 blocks away, Moonstruck at 38 x 4th Ave, absolutely worth a visit! And of course a Pax at the corner of Bryant Park, so no need to go hungry.
We loved our stay, and I would love to stay here again! But: it is a budget hotel, so don’t come expecting the Ritz!

“mildew and pubic hair but close to times square” This hotel is near Times Square and all the touristy action. It's also on a major intersection and is a low-rise building, so expect lots of noise when you're sleeping. The window was broken which made for a cold breezy evening in November. (Heat not yet on). The bathroom had lots of mildew and pubic hair. It was the same pubic hairs from one day to the next. Do they not clean? I am a big fan of low budget places and hostels, but I wouldn't stay here again.

“The bare minimum, but that's OK!” I stayed at the Americana Inn during a conference. The Inn is ideally located and a great bargain. The Inn was clean. As typical for most NY Hotels, the rooms were a bit small. Nevertheless, I recommend the Americana Inn for budget travelers.

“Great value and location” When I stayed at this hotel I was a student and didn't have means to stay in a more expensive hotel hence this one was ideal.
I found this hotel to be very good value. Its location was good, with a short walk to Times Square, 5th Avenue shops, Macy's, near the subway etc. The hotel did not provide breakfast, but there are good deli's and coffee shops near by.
The rooms had shared bathrooms, but I had no problems getting hot water whatever time of day and the bathrooms and bedrooms were clean and in good condition
For when I was in the hotel room, it was a single room, which was a little small. But the air con worked and the TV had plenty of stations.
No issues with excess noise and the staff were very friendly and helpful.
If you want luxury or are honeymooning, this may not be the place for you. However, if you are on a budget it is ideal.
It did its job well and if money was an issue I would not hesitate in staying there again.

“After a reservation snafu, a decent stay” Things definitely didn't get off on the right foot when I got there and found out that my reservation had been cancelled. It was probably partially my own fault, since I had inquired the day before about cancellation policies because a friend was waffling about going with me, but they were able to put me in a single room (316) that served its purpose.
As many have said, it does have an institutional feel. It almost felt like a college dorm. The room was very basic but surprisingly big for a single, with a twin bed, dresser (both on the worn side)and a decent-sized closet. Aside from some stray hairs (not mine) on the floor and a three-day old NY Times under the bed, it was very clean, as was the bathroom. I was also surprised how quiet it was...you'd hear the occasional door slam or people walking around, but nothing major at all.
I do have to compliment the staff, who were very accomodating and friendly, especially during check-in.
I wish we had the ability to do half-star ratings on here, since it's actually closer to three-and-a-half level...nothing remarkable but well-maintained and especially well-staffed.

“Splendid location, good value for money” Well, u know what u pay for. $120 on Manhattan is considered "cheap" (it was incredible to me too but only before I started to book an affordable accommodation in NYC) even if there is shared bathtub. Sure, u may pay some extra $50 per night to have your own shower. But what for? I mean - no problem at all in Am.Inn, bathrooms (3 on each floor for only ~10 rooms of this floor) were always free. Water pressure is not proper but okay. 
The main feature (and simply unrivalled) is LOCATION. Which is simply perfect as u r right in the centre of everything.
However single room is not for claustrophobic travelers - it was the tiniest one I ever seen, exactly size of normal wardrobe. And pubic hair was discovered somewhere, but as u r 2 min from 5th Avenue maybe it's not so awful...But TV ran normally.

“Great location, good value, go stay at the Americana Inn!” Ignore the whiney comments from my fellow Brits below!
Americana Inn is an excellent budget hotel, located in midtown, just a few blocks away from Times Square, Madison Square Garden / Penn Station and the Empire State Building - and just a 2 minute walk away from Macys and the Manhattan Mall. And a couple blocks away from entrances to 2 subway stations (Bryant Park, and Herald Square). 
I've stayed in New York City a few times, in a variety of places, always on a budget. I know how expensive the city is to stay in, so to find a safe, clean, central hotel like this is a huge bonus, and I will stay there again. 
You couldn't get a better location, and the hotel feels very safe, and it was spotlessly clean when I stayed there. Sure, it's shared bathrooms, but you share one between about 4 rooms, and they are newly refurbished and very clean.
As for the room - I stayed in a single room, and it was just fine. Not big of course, but to be honest - bigger than I expected from reading some reviews! There was storage space, a sink, and enough room for 1 comfortably. 
And yes it's noisey - as many of the rooms look over 6th avenue. But hey, it's NYC for goodness sakes, what do people expect! Take ear plugs - or buy them from Duane Reade drug store, there is one just down the road from the Americana. They really do make a heck of a difference. 
My only negative comment would be - the hotel advertises Cable TV - but whether it was just my room, or a general problem - the TV did not work well. The majority of channels where messed up. And all you could pick up clearly was a few local NY channels. Now it didn't make a huge difference to me, as I wasn't in my room enough to want a TV much. But if the hotel is going to advertise this, then really it should make sure it works. 
But all in all, a really good hotel, and I would recommend it highly to those on a budget. A single room there costs around $70 a night, which for the location is excellent.

“Perfect Hotel Perfect Location” Excellent hotel. All the reviews say the same, excellent. If you find fault with this hotel for any reason, other than the cable stations which are limited, you should be staying at the Waldorf. In New York City this price usually gets you many many things, mostly bugs. This hotel is clean, clean, clean. Thanks guys.

“The basics on the Upper West Side” In short, a condensed experience! Bathroom was brand new, clean and well lighted -- just tiny. The room and hallways were relatively quiet, though spaces are narrow -- I can imagine someone who is claustrophobic might not enjoy their stay. Staff were friendly and efficient, and safe neighborhood, with nearest subway one block south on Broadway, offering convenient transportation and shopping.

“Nice enough if the price is right” I got a pretty good deal of 129 a night, so it was adequate. The room was small but very clean, the reception area also small but nice, a little retro-chic that's probably original. Front desk personnel very helpful and the internet was free, very nice. Great neighborhood for eating, shopping, subway access, close to the park. When I checked again for staying a week later on a return trip the price was double, in which case it would not be anywhere near a decent value. So, check it out and don't be afraid to choose this place if the price is decent.
They did have some sort of off-putting signs something to the effect of if you are one minute past the noon check-out they'll have you thrown in debtor's prison, but I was leaving early so it didn't become an issue. Still, not a very welcoming attitude, that.

“Very disappointing” I had a quick stay in New York before returning home and chose this because of the price. I was extremely disappointed with it. The room was tiny (not an issue really) but the biggest issue was the noise. There was a generator or something under my room which started every hour, all through the night and kept waking me up. Also, anyone who happened to be on the corridor outside the room could be heard as if they were in the room beside me. Very unimpressed with the hotel.

“Terrific hotel, small, but excellent for the price” I can't list any complaints about the Belnord Hotel. For those who lament its small size, what in the world are you in NYC for? It's all about being outside of the hotel, exploring and enjoying the City's sites. 
Sure, the rooms are small. Our room had a full-size bed that my 6'4" husband had a bit of trouble keeping his feet on. But it wasn't a nuisance, and there was a good-size flat-screen TV and a small, compact closet to store our stuffs in. The bathroom was teeny-tiny but good enough for our needs.
Overall, the hotel was easy to find, clean, efficient, and offered a great price. The one complaint I had was about the luggage storage room. They don't check to see if you're even staying in the hotel before they give you the key to it. All of our stuff stayed secure enough, though, so I suppose I should give them the benefit of the doubt.
This is a great place just to crash, and just one block from the subway. Excellent location for families, especially if you're hopping on over to Central Park or the local museums.

“Teeny, Tiny Room” The bath room was clean, the service was adequate,the air conditioning worked in the heat wave, location just what I wanted but the room was the smallest hotel room I've eve seen. When I called to ask if a roll away could be put in the room because my son decided to join me I was told that they "don't do rollaways". What they didn't tell is that the room is so small a roll away won't fit. Still laughing......

“Remember this is New York...” The rooms are TINY here. So when you open the door you almost hit the bed LOL. But its good for 2 people if not staying too long. No space at all. But its good location. Quiet for being NY and clean. Internet also available

“A-mazing!” Loved my stay here. Room and bathroom were really clean. The room was small but I didn't mind side I only needed a place to sleep. Subway is only a block away which can take you to where all the attractions are in 10 min. Will defenetly go back!

“excellent value” if you need a lot of space try the holiday inn,,,,if you want a great deal in nyc stay here....small rooms , I only sleep there, great location, quiet, clean and cheap for nyc with tax $140 ish.......

“Great price/location, small room” Husband and I stayed 4 nights at the Belnord on our 6th trip to the City. Fantastic location! But be forewarned that folks aren't kidding when they say the rooms are SMALL. It was okay with me, I'm 5'8" 150 lbs. Husband is 5'10" 200 lbs and he felt the room was too small for him. Bathroom nicely sized. We always found the room and the hotel to be clean. NO bedbugs ~ whew! The price was why we tried the Belnord - best price for accommodations we could find.

“Definitely worth it for the price” Rates were very reasonable. Facility was clean. Staff was polite.
Room was quite small, but big enough for two people to stay in. You might not want to stay here if you were going to be in the room all the time, but you should be able to find enough going on in New York city to occupy your waking hours....
Bathrooms were shared, but there were four on the floor we were staying and we never had problems getting into one.
Be advised the hotel does not have an elevator.

“Comfortable Stay” This hotel is great for a business trip or short stay. The staff is excellent, room comfortable and clean, and breakfast delicious. However, the bathroom sink is set too far away (close to the mirror) and it was not easy to lean so far forward to use the sink.

“Best Garden Inn I've ever stayed in!” Exceptionally clean and friendly. The breakfast buffet is top notch; amazing selections and the service was friendly and perfect. Every employee in this hotel was warm and helpful and genuinely seemed to enjoy their job, which is reflected in all the details that made this hotel so nice. I've stayed in many Garden Inns, and this is by far the nicest. We will be back for sure when we visit family!

“Nice HGI in Houston” Was on business trip in Houston seeing various clients. I chose this HGI as HP (my last client visit) was a quick drive from here and Tripadvisor had positive reviews. 
Checked in late on a Monday evening and was given my room card. The hotel looked new and was clean. Had a king sized bed which was comfortable. Wifi in the room worked fine. Did not use the gym or the breakfast due to time. I did use the business center to print up my boarding passes for the next day.
Receipt was under my door in the morning and was accurate.
Room rate was just under $200 which I thought was a bit expensive for the area.

“Great hotel for the business traveler” One of the nicest Hilton Garden Inns I've had the pleasure to stay on business travel. Good on-site restaurant and great front desk staff. Free use of nearby 24 hour Lifetime Fitness facility.

“Very nice staff and property” I stayed here for three nights and was not disappointed. The rooms were nice, well appointed and all of the things I expect at a Hilton Garden Inn. There are many restaurants nearby and they offer a very good breakfast.

“Yet another great Hilton Garden Inn” This property ranks high on my list as one of the nicest HGIs I've ever stayed. Very nice, well-cared-for place. The staff is very friendly, helpful, and courteous. The restaurant is top notch. The work-out room has everything an exerciser might want. Computers and printers in the business center all worked. It's located along a busy highway, but I don't recall the traffic noise as a major problem, even though I had a highway-side room. The location was not necessarily good for me, but I can't count that factor against the place because of the nature of my job. Convenient hotels in Tomball just don't stack up, quality-wise. I don't mind driving a bit farther to stay in a nice place, especially on the northwest side of Houston. If you feel obligated to go out to eat away from the hotel, you will have plenty of choices, even within walking distance.

“A nice hotel” I have stayed there many times and even once left a bad review. This hotel is a very nice property. We paid $39 a night through Priceline. It is always clean, and the entry way is pretty. The staff always has a little bit of an attitude. I think it may be because the only times I am ever there is for soccer tournaments, and all those kids can make an adult a little cranky. I heard several of the staff arguing with parents who were asking for late checkouts on the last day of play. I remember having the same problem before, but it was not an issue for me this time. I heard quite a few parents complaining who were not with our team. I heard the front desk staff telling people that no more than two rooms per team could have a late checkout. I also heard the front desk staff talking negatively about parents as they left. A bit unprofessional. Personally, my only complaint was that I did not get the double beds that I called and asked for. I called about 5 days before my arrival, and they confirmed that the room would be double/double. I know with Priceline there is no guarantee on what kind of room you get, but I was a bit disappointed. They did, however, provide a king room with a couch pullout. It worked just fine for us although the couch was a bit uncomfortable. The food is always good at the restaurant, and the pool was adequate. This hotel is nicely situated for soccer tournaments that take place at the Spring fields, and it is very close to Willowbrook mall. The parking is also free.

“Wonderful choice!” Great location next to P.F. Changs restaurant. Hotel offered an inexpensive buffet breakfast each day (for surcharge) which included cooked to order omelets. The pool area is large and includes a hot tub. Complimentary wifi, coffee, and parking also included in price. For late nights, there is a bar/restaurant right in front of the hotel that is open late. They have live music on some nights.

“Clean and Convenient” I chose this hotel because of its proximity to a social function we were going to and because I am Hilton Honors member. The hotel is clean and the rooms are spacious. It has all the conveniences I expect for business travel.

“Have always found this HGI to be a great choice !” I've stayed at this property at least 3 times in the last year or so. I have found them to be consistent in a good way with cleanliness, service, etc. The rooms are your typical HGI rooms with the little fridge and microwave. The bathroom is a nice size with quite a bit of counter space. The location is convenient to Cypress Fairbanks Hospital, Willow Brook Mall and another nice shopping area. A number of restaurants are close by and there is a PF Chang's less than a block away. 
On my most recent visit there was some type of high school tournament in town (rugby or soccer) and the hotel was full of high school boys and parents. Frankly, lots of the parents were in the bar more than they were watching their kids -- but -- the hotel staff did a great job of stopping all of the elevator and hallway "running and jumping" that was going on while the parents were in the bar. The weekends are usually pretty quiet though.
Would stay here again -

“Not Quite the basics for a business traveler” Although the location is good for getting downtown, and although there's a great seafood restaurant close by (Goode's) the minimal fitness center was a disappointment. As always the staff is terrific.

“Great place for an extended stay” Free parking and breakfast. Full size fridge, microwave, dishes, dish washer, pool, tennis courts. If you are looking for a long ter,m place to stay this is a good one. Great location with free highway access. There is a courtyard next door which I prefer for shorter stays. There was also a pull out couch bed.
“Great stay!!” Had a great stay at the Residence Inn. The breakfast was excellent and the front desk staff was super friendly and helpful. Will stay there again when we visit Houston.

“Clean, fabulous location, overpriced” It's clean, the rooms are large, and the location--for a business traveler--can't be beat. But not worth the rack rate (over $180/nite) so stay only if you get a deal here.

“Nice Rooms but Shady Managment” May 2010. We had the opportunity to spend several nights at this property when we were in the area. The hotel off of a side road off of the toll way. Be careful about driving on the toll way or you could get fined $25.00 each way. I recommend staying off of it. This property is near Rice University, the Galleria is not too far by car and it is near the River Oaks area of Hourston. There is plenty of free parking in the parking lot. 
Check-in was very fast but I knew something was wrong when the front desk person take my Marriott Bonus Bucks coupon. 
Our room was comfortable and your standard Big Box Residence Inns. The bed was comfortable. Lighting in the room was good. , The work desk was moderate and the office-style chair okay.. My The room had a sleeper sofa and a comfortable arm chair.
 The bathroom was clean.. Lighting was good, the towels were plentiful, and the shower worked well – immediate hot water with plenty of pressure. Bath amenities include shampoo, conditioner, lotion/
The breakfast buffet featured scrambled eggs, hot oatmeal, and all the other things you would expect on a breakfast buffet.
The hotel public areas were clean and well-kept, but could use an updating to the style of the rooms. 
When checking out and settling my bill, the front desk management processed Marriott Travel cards first before the Residence Inn Bonus Bucks. This left with a difficult choice because if I used the Bonus Bucks I would not able to use the face value. This is awful strange since on this trip the Residence Inn at Alamo Square in San Antonio had no problem accepting the full amount of the Bonus Buck. Also after this trip I used a Marriot property bonus buck at the Renaissance Madison in Seattle and they had no problem accepting it. I had used a Bonus Buck at the J.W. Marriott Union Square in San Francisco and they had no problem accepting it. This property and it's managment was sneaky in what it did just to make a few bucks!
I have a future trip scheduled for Houston and it is fair to stay I won't be staying at this property again!

“Good central location” We ended up with a studio suite and it was plenty enough space for the four of us. The front desk receptionist was very sweet and very apologetic (Travelocity pulled a number on us) but the clerk did whatever she could to appease us. We have one teenager and one 9 year old and we had a queen sized bed and a double sized sofabed and we were comfortable. The sofabed wasn't lumpy and didn't sag in the middle so it must've been fairly new. The full kitchen including a full sized refrigerator was a bonus. We could stock up on items like soda and water from the H.E.B., CVS or Kroeger's around the corner. The room was clean and it seemed like everything was in good working order - toilet, shower, sinks, fridge, etc. The swiveling flatscreen t.v. was something we all took advantage of. Hermann Park and the museum district are within a few minutes drive and so was downtown and the Galleria. We were there during Thanksgiving weekend so there was no traffic, but on normal business days you could potentially encounter traffic, especially downtown, but it was a good central location to all of the sites. I understand M.D. Anderson is also nearby and the hotel offers a free shuttle there if you need it, but we didn't use it so I can't comment on it. The breakfast buffet is a good way to start your day. The menu changes but includes a meat (sausage or bacon), eggs on some days (although my daughter commented that it doesn't taste like real eggs), pancakes and doughnuts on some days, and there was always oatmeal, several types of cereals, fruit, yogurt, texas sized and shaped waffles you make yourself, milk (chocolate, 2% and skim), juice (cranberry, grapefruit, orange), muffins, bagels, english muffins, and coffee/tea. They were constantly replacing empty pans so you could go at anytime and they never ran out of anything. We had other meals elsewhere but there is a Chili's within walking distance of the hotel as well as other places within a quick car ride. We spent 3 days here and enjoyed our stay. I recommend it for something inexpensive yet comfortable that is in a good location to go museum/zoo hopping.

“Great Place to Stay” My wife and I stayed in a studio suite at the Residence Inn-Houston West University for two nights/three days recently and we both thought the place was great. Although we arrived early (12:15 p.m.) the staff went ahead and allowed us to check in. Our room was spacious and had a kitchen with full size stove, refrigerator, plates utensils, etc.; desk with computer internet connection; living room area with 32-inch flat screen TV; "bedroom" just off the living room area with a queen size bed; a dressing area with a sink; and a tiled bathroom . Furniture and linens were showing a little wear and tear but were just fine. The entire place was very clean. The hotel has a pool and hot tub, small exercise room, and a business center with several computers and printers. I have to say that the included breakfast was one of the best I have ever had at a motel and included everything you could think of including oatmal, cereals, many types of breads and donuts, scrambled eggs, sausage, fried potatoes, french toast, waffels, juices, coffee, yogurt, milk, fruit and lots of other stuff. The hotel is located a street south of US-59 and was a little difficult to get to from US-59 (even though I had a map and knew where the hotel was located) because traffic on Buffalo Speedway makes it difficult to turn east onto Westpark Drive (the road the hotel is located on). Plus the signage for the hotel is very small and hard to see. No big deal - just a warning to bring a map with you. Also, the Courtyard Motel is located on the front of the property and the Residence Inn on the back so you will need to drive to the Residence Inn sign near the back of the property to check in. The hotel location is fantastic and is close to Rice University, the Museum District, several farmers markets, lots of restaurants and shopping, a very nice HEB Grocery store, US-59, and the Galleria. Parking was free which is a big deal because most other hotels in this area charge approx $10.00 per day to park. The Residence Inn-Houston West University was a great place to stay and we will definitely stay here again while in the area.

“Very good accommdations if you need to be in this area -- with one exception” I stayed at the Residence Inn because it was convenient to a hospital where a friend was being treated. Not a scenic location by any stretch of the imagination, but it's good if you are staying at a nearby medical facility. Many restaurants nearby. The staff were extremely friendly, professional and solicitous. When they didn't know the answer to something, they tried to find out. The room was very clean. I got an upgrade to a two room suite with my Marriott rewards card, although I don't have that many points on the card -- I just asked. Unlike some residence hotels, the kitchen was stocked with cooking utensils, plates, dish washing soap, etc. Windows are locked shut, but they had someone unlock them for me. Bathroom amenities are find. Good water pressure on shower. Huge selection of food for breakfast, some good quality (e.g., fresh fruit), some not so much (e.g., packaged donuts). Very comfortable dining area. Computers were not always working, but the sister hotel next door allows guests to use theirs, including printer -- no fee. Nice outdoor pool. Here was the problem: When I arrived at the Houston airport, I took a taxi to the hotel. At my departure, I asked the front desk clerk call me a taxi to the airport. When the car arrived, the clerk informed me that it was a car service that would be cheaper and "safer" than a taxi. First of all, it was more expensive for a shorter drive (flat rate of $65). Second, I'm concerned if hotel staff don't feel that taxis in the area are safe. I did comment to Marriott on their web site and received what I feel is an unsatisfactory answer: that they have some kind of arrangement with the car service and that they were not aware that it cost more. This was not a big blip for an otherwise good experience.

“Not my favorite Residence Inn” Four of us spent an overnight here recently in a one bedroom unit. We chose it because it was close to family and a reasonable price given the area. It was an okay place to stay, but certainly not great.
On the plus side, the breakfast was excellent, the place was clean, furniture and decor were lovely and the people at the front desk were pleasant. 
On the negative, we felt very cramped in our 1 bedroom unit. The bedroom was small and the living area seemed smaller. Even the common breakfast area in the lobby was cramped and crowded. (The hotel itself is HUGE. Walking to breakfast seemed to take 10 minutes.) The pool area was also crowded.
Also on the negative - no wireless internet and local phone calls cost $.50. (Why can't they give free local calls? This is such a small thing, but it irritated us.) Additionally, it is difficult to find. (It's the same driveway as the Courtyard, but in the back and you can't necessarily see it from the feeder.)
It does seem like the positives should outweigh the negatives I listed, but somehow, for our group, being in such close quarters was a huge negative. 
If the price was right we might consider staying here again, but never for more than one night.

“Great Hotel!” Althought the hotel is poorly marked and a little tough to find, it is well worth it!
Clean rooms, warm pool, friendly staff, tasty breakfast!
I would definately stay here again!

“Great location, super clean, only bad thing shared bathrooms” My sister and I stayed at Hotel Alexander to visit Columbia University. The room was bigger than we expected, although it was a double bed. We had 2 closets in the room, a desk and a chair and a TV. We had problems the first day getting the space heater on but I asked in the reception and the room was nice and warm after that. The room was clean and the bathroom too. I saw the cleaning lady cleaning the bathroom several times a day and when I used it it was clean. BYO soap, you have hand soap in the room but not in the bathroom.
The location in Upper West Side was excellent, residential area very quiet and close to the subway station. The staff was attentive and called a cab for us when we were going to NJ. Even thoguh it was more expensive than a hostel, it was worth it. Clean rooms, clean bathrooms and a safe area. I would definitely stay here again.

“The Hotel Alexanderin New York – good price but noisy with cockroachs” The hotel is really a cross between a hostel and a hotel but is good value if don’t care about noise from doors slamming in the hall all nights and cockroach. The service at the front desk was poor. 
We found cockroach every night and morning we stayed there. We asked many times at the front desk to do something about it without success.
There were doors in our hallway that slammed shut every time someone came through all night.
The local neighbourhood is great with cafes, diners, delis, convenience stores and restaurants.
Our room was cheap and clean, so if you're looking not to spend a lot and aren't expecting a lot, this place will be perfect. I know next time I go to the City, I will pay a little more to stay in a nicer hotel.

“Good NYC alternative” We were looking for a reasonable place to stay in Manhatten and this seemed a good bet. We chose the renovated room with two Queen beds and were very pleased with the comfort and cleanliness. Hostel prices but better quality. We phoned ahead to inform them that we would arrive in the middle of the night and they held our room as promised and checked us in at 2am. The desk staff on duty throughout our staff were always friendly. I don't believe they have a full maintenance staff so when we had no hot water in our private bath, we were forced to use the shared facility because there were no other comparable rooms available and we didn't want to give up our two beds. Short of running into dripping people wrapped scantily in towels, running between shared shower and their rooms, we had no real complaints. The neighborhood is safe and quiet and restaurant selection is wide. Proximity to Riverside Park, Central Park and the subway are all nice features.

“AMAZING AND CHEAP!!” After reading the reviews I was a little worried about staying here. Well the hotel turned out to be AWESOME. Yes, this might not be your five star hotel, but if you are on a budget this hotel is for you. The room was clean and the bed was comfy enough. I was surprised on how clean the bathroom was which was shared with a few other rooms on the floor. The area is safe and the hotel is a block away from the subway station. There is a CVS, RiteAid and a bunch of restaurants within walking distance too. Overall I had a wonderful experience and will definitely stay there again.

“Great hotel on a budget” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Hotel Alexander on our first trip to NYC. After trawling the web for reasonably priced, well located hotels in Manhattan, we stumbled across this one and were very happy we did.
The staff were attentive and friendly, the room was clean and comfortable, and the price was reasonable. 
It wasnt a five star establishment - but then it doesnt claim to be. For the most part, when we're traveling overseas, all a hotel needs to be is safe and clean - somewhere to rest while exploring the city. Hotel Alexander was great for this - we always felt welcome, always felt safe, and it was in a great location - close enough to everything to get to where we wanted to go without much hassle, but far enough away that we could escape the 'city' while we recharged.
A great place, would definitely stay there again.

“Trendy and original” This is a very unique hotel that is not part of the chain. It is trendy and modern. I'm no interior designer but I could tell they had some serious and expensive work done. The lobby was small but very artistic. Interesting sofa, table, lamps, wall... like from catalogue. They made good use of that little space. Elevators are clean and fast. Room was small like all the rooms in Manhattan but it was very cozy and practical. It had great bed, high quality sheets and comforter, new TV, warm colors and lot of light. We actually ended up staying in - it was so nice. 
Service was exceptional. We got the wake up call, directions, recommendations for restaurant, etc. Hotel had lively bar which we used for little bit. Location was the best about this hotel. Even though it was little bit difficult to find it due to not very visible entrance), we came to appreciate how close to everything hotel was. We could walk everywhere including Times Square. Definitely stay here! You will get the outside of box experience.

“good deal & great location” It was very clean and worth the cheap price. The bathrooms were always cleaned through out the day. Loads of shopping and dining in the area. Your right at the 1 train and the M104 bus. They take into time square and the UN. 
This was my first hostel experience in the states. I have no compliaints. I knew that for such a low price you would get necessities only. Very nice staff also. 
If your coming to nyc to have fun and stay busy this location could work because you'd have more money for shopping, seesightseeing, dining, walking to Central Park., close to Empire Hotel who has a great free lounge and rooftop bar. 
I will difinitely us it again and recommend it to friends that come here for a week or weekend of fun.

"Upper West Side hotel" The room was small but clean. The structure seemed like two buildings that had been connected later. The surrounding area was calm. I did not feel unsafe even at night. On the walk from the subway station there were supermarkets, drugstores, and restaurants, so it was very convenient.

"Well located, but without any comfort" Together with my daughter (15 years old), I was planning a short city trip to New York. What mattered to us was a good hotel location (which it had, on the Upper West Side) and a low price (not exactly easy in New York). You cannot hope for comfort in this place. The staff is friendly (I suspect they are students at the reception desk) and helpful (calling a taxi, lending a hairdryer free of charge). The room was reasonably clean, but in miserable condition. The door to a small adjoining room, which turned out to be a construction site and was apparently meant to become a bathroom someday, was damaged. The window facing an air shaft would not close properly, and the heat was barely lukewarm despite freezing outdoor temperatures, so we were cold at night. The shared bathroom in the hallway was fairly clean, but urgently needed renovation and was also ice cold.

"Good value for money for New York" We chose this hotel because it was one of the cheapest places we found in New York that had a private bathroom and was not a shared room. About 70 euros per night when booking in advance on the hotel's website. 
I had read reviews saying there were bedbugs and that it was very dirty, but I was able to confirm that there were no bedbugs and, fortunately, it was very clean. They cleaned the room and bathroom every day. The room was small, but it had a good bed and a bathroom that, although small, was quite functional. 
We were a little cold because the heat sometimes did not work. Later the front desk explained that the heating was not controlled by the hotel, but by the city of New York, which turns it on or off depending on how cold it is. 
Breakfast was not included, and I cannot comment on it because there were many bakeries nearby where we had very good breakfasts. The hotel did offer free coffee. 
Wi-Fi is free, but you have to go down to the TV lounge because it does not reach the rooms.
It is quite far from the center, so you need to take the subway, which is about a 5-minute walk away. 
All in all, a good hotel to sleep in.

“Not a Glitch Free Stay” Hampton Inn Columbus-Easton is pretty much like all the others properties in my favorite mid-range hotel group, although this particular location doesn’t rate as one of the best, in my eyes, at least. After a very pleasant and quick check-in, I went to my room and immediately had trouble connecting to the Internet, a problem the hotel staff itself couldn’t solve. A quick call to the toll free number on the desk provided a solution in seconds, a simple matter the hotel folks should have known about. The wall-mounted temperature controller in my room displayed the temperature only in Centigrade, another problem the staff couldn’t fix. There was no safe in the room – always an issue for a business traveler. Overall construction seemed a bit shabby - for example, the surprisingly low quality sliding glass shower doors (no tubs in most of the rooms) were broken, coming apart and dangerously sharp. Equally sharp were the corners of the night tables next to the bed; I badly bruised myself getting out of bed one night. The windows are sealed in Easton and can’t be opened! I’m a fresh air freak and that’s a deal breaker for me. The elevators seemed slower than usual, but who knows. The staff was friendly and as helpful as they could be without solving my problems. The business center worked perfectly, and although I didn’t sample it, I saw that the free breakfast was Hampton all the way. In the end and in spite of the problems, I had another couple of peaceful nights in a comfortable Hampton Inn bed. Bottom line: I’m still a fan of the chain but Columbus-Easton is a Hampton Inn property I would think twice about visiting again.

“Excellent Stay” My daughter and I stayed here for 4 nights when we took in a concert in Columbus, but decided on staying in Easton as we intended to spend more time shopping than anything else. The shuttle from the airport was very quick and we had excellent drivers both ways. Check-in was very efficient and we were greeted warmly and within a few minutes we were in our room. Very spacious and clean - at first glance the beds looked terribly lumpy... turns out it was just the style of duvets they use and it was all very comfortable indeed. The comp breakfast was a good start to the day and fresh coffee was available all day from the breakfast area. Would definately recommend this hotel.

“Good value, great location.” Stayed here for business in late October 2011. Relatively new Hampton property, about 15 minutes drive from downtown Columbus. Standard Hampton Breakfast and amenities, clean and well maintianed with pleasant staff.
There is a gas station/convenience store next door and a large mall with plenty of dining options a mile or two away.
Since I was flying I was choosing between this Hampton and the one at the airport and was very happy with my decision. The ride to the airport was quick and easy.

“Great hotel, will stay again” I received superior service, from every agent at the front desk. I was always greeted, whether I was coming in or leaving. I was immediately acknolwedged, even if I needed to wait because someone was in line in front of me. The staff attitude was always enthusiastic and upbeat, from the maids to the managers. I stay in a lot of hotels due to business and pleasure trips, and I must say whoever is in charge of customer service here is doing it right. I attended a conference for a part time business that I run, so this was partially business and pleasure combined. For my full time job I stay in hotels consistently, generally more upscale. But I must say I would not hesitate to stay in or recommend this hotel regardless of the reason you are in town. I chose this hotel over another where my convention was taking place because I read overwhelmingly negative reviews about that property. Reviews of and location of this Hampton Inn made my decision. 
I am a stickler for cleanliness, and this hotel did not disappoint. The public areas were immaculate, and the room was very clean. It has a modern upgraded feel. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The lights in the bathroom go on automatically when you enter. The bed, as others have said was very comfortable.
Breakfast was always attractively presented in a bight breakfast room and I never saw spills or crumbs although there was not a lot of staff seen in the area. There is a waffle maker there every day, along with presentations of fresh and cut fruit, bagels, muffins pastries, cereals, milk (including skim) and coffee,tea and juices. There were always an additional two hot items (sausage patties and cheese omelets one day, scrambled eggs and sausage gravy another day, scrambled eggs with ham and maple smoked sausage on a third day). The eggs are some powdered mixture, but same as you'd get anywhere. They're acceptable. If you are in a hurry and want breakfast to go they have bags at the front desk that at the time contained a granola bar, apple, bottle of water and muffin. A very nice assortment.
There is a gas station and convenience store sharing the parking lot (it is very convenient and not obtrusive at all. A shopping center across the street with Wal Mart, Hometown Buffet and several stores, and of course Easton Town Center, a lovely indoor and outdoor shopping center with a variety of things to do. I enjoyed the comedy club and a few of the restaurants on my own. Also includes a nice movie theater and free outdoor entertainment in the summer when I visited.
I saw every time of guest, from families to individuals in business suits. I get the sense this property is recommended a lot, and I would not hesitate to stay again.

“Will stay here for every conference in Columbus!” Four of us stayed at this hotel for a conference in Columbus area, booked a 2 QUEEN BEDS STUDIO SUITE W/ SOFABED NONSMOKING room & had PLENTY of room for all of us, our wardrobes, belongings, & shopping items. Great staff, SUPER clean rooms, hotel, delicious breakfast & even a bagged breakfast if you can't/don't have time for the hot breakfast. Had an issue with our first room having a very strong smell (like smoke and a chemical "smoke smell remover" had been used--one of us have a high sensitivity to sensory allergy triggers and the staff at the Hampton Inn moved us without question and verified there were no present odors in the new room. Another reason we'll always choose Hampton Inn! Great value!!

“Book Now!” My husband has a busniness meeting in Columbus, so I wanted to stay near things I could do,in his absence. This hotel met all our needs, and Exceeded them, on every level! The staff, including the lovely front desk clerk who gave me her St Pat's Day green beads, because I had no green on (I didnt get her name, but she is so sweet and helpful!), to John, the gentleman who drives you to the Easton Mall in the shuttle, and actually everyone we encountered here, are wonderful!
We booked a King suite, and the extra room was great; more like a small studio apartment;sparkling clean room, bath, great work desk,sitting area, and cozy bed. The breakfast the next day was very nice, lots of choices, and I was able to get some exercise in, walking the short, safe distance to the WalMart and other shops beside the hotel.
Management and staff are to be Highly commended for excellent customer service, the location is great, and we definitely plan to stay here again, when we come to the Columbus area. Book with total confidence that your stay will be a true pleasure!

“Good Location, Great Staff” I was in Columbus on business in early April, and this was one of several hotels in the Easton area where I needed to stay. I picked this particular one based on the rate and pictures / descriptions found on the hotel's website. 
It's a newer property, so that helps with things like design, cleanliness, and amenities. The basic HI&S layout includes a bigger nicer dining room/lobby area, and then a really nice fitness center (4 treadmills, a couple of other machines, and a weight machine) next to the pool and hot tub. All three were at the front of the hotel with windows all across the front, so it not only looked good but was also very light which was nice. There was also a business center with 3 workstations and a laundry facility right off the lobby.
This is a Hampton Inn AND Suites, so I know not all rooms are suites, but I was really surprised at how small my room was. It didn't really affect my stay, but this room was much smaller in comparison to other Hamptons at which I've stayed - kind of surprising, especially for a newer hotel. Also, the room didn't have a luggage rack or do not disturb card for the door - don't know if that was the case for all rooms or if these items were simply missing. But the room had what I needed - a king-size bed, working desk not next to the AC Unit, FREE Internet, and a decent-sized bathroom (although no bath tub, one of those double-sized showers with the 2" floor and sliding glass doors - not the usual tub w/ curved shower curtain combo).
The breakfast staff and maintenance staff in particular were extremely friendly and professional, seemed genuinely happy to be there. It made the breakfast portion of the stay enjoyable. It was pretty busy and packed both mornings, but never had to wait for a clean table or for food - it was always very well and continuously stocked. They kept things moving without rushing anyone. Also, there is a little snack "shop" right behind the front desk - that was great if you didn't have time for breakfast or wanted to get something small to eat/drink without leaving the hotel (although they do have a shuttle to take you to the mall). The front desk provided several menus from close local restaurants that would deliver dinner - the recommendation (Italian/pizza restaurant in Gahanna) was great.
Net it out - it was a good stay; appreciated the cleanliness and friendly staff, the location (lot of shops - Easton "Mall" close by, and also only about 5 minutes from the airport) and the fitness center. I'd definitely stay here again if I'm in the area.

“A great place to host a meeting and stay within budget” I just hosted a two day meeting at the Hampton Inn and Suites in the Easton area. Great facilities for a group of 30 employees. The staff was service oriented and worked hard to make sure that the meeting went smooth! We were able to cater lunch and breaks from the outside which really helped bring this meeting in budget. With the hotel situated next to the Easton shopping complex, the evenings offered something for everyone. An absolute go-to place for my next meeting in Columbus!

“Great hotel” I had to make a reservation one morning for an out of town business stay that evening. I had just stayed at another Hampton Inn while on vacation, so decided to try that brand again.
On arrival, the check in process went smoothly. The lobby was very nicely decorated and the breakfast area was big, clean and nicely decorated. The room was very nice and modernly decorated. It was comfortable and the bathroom was nice.
The only downside was when I needed to use a computer and went to the business center and there was a family using all 3 computers. After dinner, I had no problem getting on the computer.
The property is about a mile or so from Easton Town Center and I didn't really feel like walking there for dinner as it is all busy roads. Easton Town Center is really nice with lots of dining options.
Probably the only downside to the Hampton Inn chain is that they don't have a restaurant or bar, but the room was definitely nice and I am glad I went with that choice.

“Large room and great location!” We had 3 people on our group attending a conference at Easton. The hotel was having their grand opening with an Ohio State theme (players in attendance and media) with free snacks and wine! We had no problem checking in and we had a suite with two queen beds and a pull out sofa bed. The room was bigger than the Hilton at Easton we had the last time we attended the conference. Rooms had a modern flair with the sink area outside the shower area. We also had a fridge. The breakfast was average. The location is just across Morse across from Easton (north of Easton).

“Loved It!!” This hotel was awesome! It's right next to the airport but you don't hear planes or anything it's a hidden gem and its a GREAT deal! It's right off one of the main highways so that is perfect, I would stay there again anytime

“Beautiful Hotel” This hotel looks brand new. It is lovely. The suites were clean, spacious and had very nice amenities. The couch is a king sleeper. The location had a pool and hot tub. The staff was very nice. The breakfast was good although very crowded on Saturday morning. The only negative was the wifi was not working properly. Great location.

“OK airport hotel” This hotel close to airport. Rooms are spacious and seem fairly clean. I have noticed the last several stays the rooms are showing a bit more wear....but overall not bad. Great breakfast. Wish had an outdoor pool. Not much around hotel but great if looking for a solid airport hotel.

“Just a great hotel for families” Our flight got into San Antonio at 9:00 and we were allowed to check-in at 10:30. 
The rooms are all suites, so you have a living room and bedroom area. The couch in the living room pulls out into a bed, so there's no problem with cramming 5 people in a room. The bathroom is a little small, but there's enough room to maneuver. 
The breakfast spread is great. Sausage, DIY waffles, eggs, etc.
We didn't use the pool or the bar, but they looked great as well.
The only knock I'd give the hotel is the entrance. There's no easy way to get into the parking lot without illegally turning left off the street. Despite being close to the airport, there wasn't a lot of noise.
If we needed to stay by the airport again, we would Definately return. I don't typically give out 5 stars to a mid-level hotel, but this one was GREAT for our needs.

“Great stay.” Stayed for two nights with 2 other couples and we were all very satisfied.
The location is convenient to both the airport and downtown. The breakfast was very good and the dining area was spacious. The property was kept clean, the staff was attentive and polite, and the price was right. The suites are a nice touch if you need a bit of privacy, and the beds were comfortable. The fitness center is modest but well kept. Be advised that the pool and hot tub (indoor) are small and the area can get crowded pretty easily. But, it was not a problem for us.

“Great hotel and great stay!!!” Couldn't have asked for a better stay. The rooms have fridge, microwave, and two televisions. The rooms were very clean, bar and restaurant in the lobby. Staff was friendly and they have a great breakfast for only $8.95. Very comfortbale beds and it is only a few minutes from the airport.

“Beautiful Hotel” MY wife and i stayed at the Cambria Suites at the airport and to me a great place to stay even though there is a huge vacant lot there that has no bearing about the hotel,the 2 fl at screen tvs were nice and you talk about the comfy bed i wish i could order one and ship home lol the staff was very friendly and informative i recommend this hotel by all means and right near the airport was a plus sorry for the late review.

“good stay” This hotel is in a great location close to lots of places to eat.The rooms are modren decor.Beds are comfortable and clean.The bathroom is small but clean.If traveling with older folks tub is quite high to get into.The front staff is not very friendly or helpful.Overall good value for the money.Pool is very small and cloudy looking did not venture to use it.

“An Excellent Debut for a new hotel” Stayed there for 2 nights for a training on business with other colleagues - because there are only 15 or so of these hotels nationwide, I was unsure what to expect. 
Wow. 
I was shocked to realize these were under the same umbrella as Choice Hotels aka Comfort Inn etc. - they are their top offering and I must say that in most aspects this was equal to most hotels I've stayed at.
The staff is tops, breakfast buffet at 9.50 is well worth it, and there's more than ample room to workout, swim, relax, or do work in the suites.
I do hope that they build more of these as I would definitely use them again.
PS - the only complaint - the hotel has a great shuttle which takes people to/from airport, Alamo Quarry shops, Witte Museum, (both of which are worthy stops), anything within 5 miles.
Downtown is 7 miles...if there's some way they did a once daily dropoff to downtown in the AM and a return trip in the PM that would save visitors a $25 cab ride...

“I don't understand the rave reviews...” The hotel opened in Oct 08 so the rooms are brand new and the two flat screen tvs are a plus to many but I don't think this hotel is worth the $117 that I spent. First of all, the view is terrible. My room overlooked a vacant parking lot and I could hear the planes from the nearby airport throughout the night. Most extended stay hotels have a free breakfast buffet but this hotel charges approximately $10 per person and I decided not to spend the money since all of the tables were filthy. Although the front desk staff was friendly at check-in, I asked for a one hour extended check-out and they were rude and said no, but you can have 15 mins. Since I am a Platinum member with Choice Hotels, I was shocked. Although I do not have the highest status which is Diamond, I cannot imagine how they treat everyone else. If you are planning a lengthy stay I would recommend the Staybridge Suites which offers a free breakfast and free laundry unlike Cambria Suites. If you can get this hotel for $40 like another reviewer mentioned then I would stay here but it's not worth the price that I paid.

“Lovely hotel, relaxing stay close to shopping and dining options” Even though our stay at Mr C got off to a bad start (the car service they arranged for us didn't show up and we had to wait around at LAX for an hour - not the hotel's fault though), the rest of it was fantastic and very enjoyable. 
First of all, Mr C is in a very handy location for anyone wanting to shop - Rodeo Drive is a 5-10 minute stroll through a pleasant neighbourhood, and the hotel's (amazing and very convenient) car service can take you to the Beverly Center, The Grove LA or the Melrose/Robertson areas. There are also plenty of fantastic dining options nearby - ranging from fine dining down to chains like Chipotle. It is also directly across the road from a Ralphs supermarket and a CVS pharmacy, which was handy for us as we always take home lots of American treats we can't get here, like Junior Mints! We've stayed previously at the Beverly Hilton and the Mosaic Beverly Hills, and I have to say I like the location of Mr C better, particularly if you're like us and enjoy walking around. 
The service is amazing - from the warm greeting (complete with delicious Bellinis), the car service chaffeurs, the bell and valet staff - everyone is friendly and nothing is a problem at all. I had the concierge make a number of dinner reservations a few weeks prior to our arrival and that was great. Put simply, you cannot fault the Mr C staff - absolutely first class. The hotel's common areas are lovely, the decor reminded me of a vintage Italian speedboat - gleaming wood everywhere and classic leather furnishings. 
We stayed in a standard room on the Pico Boulevard side, on a lower floor. The room itself was spacious, very clean and decorated beautifully with a small furnished balcony overlooking Pico and the pool area. We did not find the room to be noisy as long as the balcony doors were closed, and found the bed to be comfortable. Housekeeping service was like clockwork twice daily, so the room was always fresh when we returned back from our explorations. Excellent selection of Cable TV channels as well, more than 50. Bathroom is compact but well equipped. 
We enjoyed dinner in the Mr C restaurant one of the nights, it is an expensive restaurant but everything we ordered was delicious and again the service was amazing, so it was well worth it for the experience. A few celebrities sighted in there as well. 
I spent one day at the pool relaxing on one of the lovely daybeds, the pool attendants are very helpful and set up a towel for you in the spot you want to sit. The pool itself is small, but the area is so nicely set up that it is very pleasant nonetheless. Pool is very clean and a good temperature. My only complaint here was that I laid out for around two hours and not once did the waitress manning the bar come to offer me a menu. In the end I went to ask for one, and after that she was attentive. I just would have expected to be asked if I needed anything, particularly as there weren't many people in there that day. 
Overall, we really enjoyed our stay at Mr C Beverly Hills and would stay there again. Great location, luxurious surroundings and great staff.

“Welcoming Luxury” Fresh, clean and solid luxury rooms. The beds are wonderful, the furniture is heavy and just feels good (leather, thick woods), and the staff is very accomodating to your every request. Love the check in process with the Bellini and personal attention. If you go, stay a few days and just sit around watching all the pretty people walk around or the gorgeous cars that pull up. While the pool area is small, they've done a good job of trying to create a relaxing zone - tip, bring your headphones and listen to music as the street behind does get a bit noisy with cars/trucks zooming by.

“An Italian enclave in LA” Nicely refurbished hotel in Beverly Hills run by the Cipriani family. The decor is italian-influenced (you can find everywhere photos of Italian actors of the 50s and 60s. Convenient location if you want to be close to Rodeo Drive. Nice view, if your rooms faces the hills. Good restaurant (Italian, what else?) but expensive. Rooms over the entrance hall can be noisy during the events. Overall, a very good stay.

“Amazing Service” The number one thing that stuck out at me was the amazing service from every single person who worked at the hotel. From the bar tender, to valet, to front desk, they all were on top of their game. I have to say the valet is one of the best I have experienced in town. They were by far the quickest at bringing my car up than any other hotel in the area. 
The rooms were nice, nothing amazing but still very nice. The bed was very comfortable, got a good nights sleep every night. The bathroom was good, with a rainfall shower and 2 sinks. There was no bathtub, just a walk in shower. The one thing I did not like was the hardwood floors in the room. You could hear the people above and beside you whenever they walked. It wasn't a huge deal but that would be the only negative about the stay. 
A few other random things...The location was great with easy access. There is a grocery store and starbucks across the street so you have everything you need within walking distance. Parking is $35 per day but that is about normal for any hotel in Beverly Hills. The complimentary wifi was a nice bonus though.

“So good, I would move to Mr. C's permanently!” Staying at Mr. C's was a very refreshng reminder of what impeccable execution and attention to detail can do.
I selected Mr. C's at the recommendation of a friend, who is a regular n the Beverly Hills area. After looking a the past reviews and the hotel's website I decided to book a premium Beverly Hills view room on a high floor.
